# Data {#sec-data}

```{r}
#| include: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

# load libraries
library(xml2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggpubr)

# load dataset
df <- read.delim('../data/JPR robbery.tab', header = T, sep="\t")
ddi <- read_xml("../data/JPR robbery-ddi.xml")   # use your file's name
xml_ns_strip(ddi)                  # removes the namespace so the paths below work

vars <- xml_find_all(ddi, ".//var")

data_dict <- data.frame(
  name  = xml_attr(vars, "name"),
  label = xml_text(xml_find_first(vars, "./labl")),
  type  = xml_attr(xml_find_first(vars, "./varFormat"), "type")
)

# clean dataset
df <- df %>% drop_na()

y <- df$lnrobberyrate
X <- as.matrix(df %>% select(!c(lnrobberyrate, llnrobberyrate, lngdpsq, country, name, period, year, flldummyrobbery)))
```

The dataset comes from Inequality and Violent Crime: Evidence from Data on Robbery and Violent Theft by Eric Neumayer [@data-paper] with the replication data found on Harvard Dataverse [@data]. Each row represents a country during a specific year. The variables of interest include:

1. the Gini coefficient,
2. the ratio of the top to bottom quintile of the income distribution,
3. the log of the gross domestic product (GDP) per capita, 
4. the growth rate of the GDP, 
5. the unemployment rate,
6. the urbanization rate,
7. the female labor force participation rate,
8. the proportion of males between the ages of 15 and 64,
9. the Polity measure of democracy,
10. the human rights violation scale, and
11. the natural log of the number of robberies and violent thefts per million people which is the response in this study.

The dataset is compiled from a variety of sources. The Gini coefficients come from the UN-WIDER database, and 6.6 is added to the values from expenditure rather than income [@data-paper]. The ratio fo the top to bottom quintile of the income distribution (data taken from A New Data Set Measuring Income Inequality by Deininger & Squire [@income-ineq]) is used to measure income inequality[@data-paper]. The rest of the data are from the UN and the World Bank [@data-paper].
